title: ci.yml's contract job cannot work — all three Aiken steps use `contracts/secuura` from the repo root, where no such directory exists; deploy-demo.yml has the same steps correct
description:
## BLUF

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` builds and tests the Aiken contracts with `cd contracts/secuura`, relative to the repo root. There is no `contracts/` at the repo root — the project is at `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` — and the workflow sets no `working-directory` and no `defaults.run.working-directory`. All three steps are wrong the same way: `aiken build` (`:205-208`), `aiken check` (`:210-213`), and the artifact path `contracts/secuura/plutus.json` (`:219`). The job would fail on the first `cd`. Latent today because Actions executes nothing on this repo, and wrong the moment it returns. The fix already exists in the tree: `deploy-demo.yml` does the identical steps with `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura`. Verified on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026.

## What was seen

Aiken appears in exactly two workflows, and they disagree.

**Broken —** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :207  — no such directory from the repo root
          aiken build

      - name: Run contract tests
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :212
          aiken check

      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: contracts/secuura/plutus.json   # :219
```

`grep -n "working-directory\|defaults:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing, so there is no job-level default to rescue the relative path.

**Correct —** `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:84-100`, same steps:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Run contract tests
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json
```

So this is a straight port of a fix that was already made once, into the file that did not get it.

## Why it matters

The contracts are the best-covered thing in platform-k and the least exercised. Measured on this commit: **10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks**, including property/fuzz modules built on `aiken-lang/fuzz` v2.2.0 (`contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23`). The only routes to running them are:

* `ci.yml` — broken as above, and dispatch-only anyway (`on: workflow_dispatch`, header *"CI/CD PIPELINE (DISABLED — DEPLOY VIA CURSOR)"*).
* `deploy-demo.yml` — correct, but fenced behind an explicit opt-in input because it targets the Azure Container Apps estate that was deleted in the 2026-07-08 cost pivot (`:35-39`, `:52-70`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` — by hand, as a deploy prerequisite.

`KS-637` (Backlog, High) already records that the nightly Internal Audit has failed 40 runs straight and that *"the Aiken tests run nowhere else"*. This ticket is the narrower, immediately-fixable half: even if a runner came back tomorrow, the general-purpose job would still fail on the `cd`, so the contract tests would still not run. On-chain validators are the one area where a regression is unrecoverable after deploy — `KS-246` (Backlog) holds the external Aiken audit as the mainnet-readiness gate, and an audit is worth much less if the suite it rests on has no working automated home.

## Suggested shape

1. Port `deploy-demo.yml`'s shape into `ci.yml`: `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` on both run steps, and `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json` as the artifact path. Three lines.
2. Consider a job-level `defaults.run.working-directory` if other steps in that job are also root-relative — worth a read of the whole job rather than patching three lines blind.
3. While there: `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` instructs the reader to `cd /Volumes/KK_DEV_Local/NEW STRUCTURE/…`, a former machine's absolute path, and recommends `aiken test` where every script and workflow in the repo uses `aiken check`. Same defect class — a documented path that cannot work anywhere but one laptop.
4. Add a contracts row to the manual-gate table in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, which has none, so `aiken check` has a named local home while Actions is down.

## Acceptance

* `ci.yml`'s contract job reaches `aiken check` from a clean checkout — provable today by running the same commands locally from the repo root, without needing a runner.
* `TESTING.md` contains no machine-specific absolute path and names `aiken check`.
* `DEV-PROCESS.md` lists the contract command with its measured wall-clock, like the 13 rows already there.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Recommend one grep across `.github/workflows/` for every root-relative `cd ` and every `path:` in an upload step, rather than fixing this instance alone. The repo moved to the `Blockchain/Dev/` layout at some point and `deploy-demo.yml` was evidently updated while `ci.yml` was not, so other files may carry the same stale assumption — and none of them can fail visibly while Actions is retired, which is exactly the condition in which this class accumulates.

## References

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:198-219` · `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:79-100` · `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/` (10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks) · `contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23` · `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` · `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` · Aiken docs: [https://aiken-lang.org/](<https://aiken-lang.org/>) · related: `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-246` (Backlog), `KS-552` (Done — the Container Apps pivot that fenced deploy-demo.yml).

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — the two workflow files were read and compared at that commit; nothing was executed and no runner was invoked. GitHub Actions on this repo answers every job with *"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed…"*, so the defect cannot surface until billing is restored.
